cases.title: Two offset boxes
cases.detail: The overlap changes at Z = 0, 2, 10 and 12. Split each section, select its regions, and rebuild caps and walls between levels.

cases.title: Box and circular cutter
cases.detail: The two vertical cuts are at Y = 5 ± √5. Circle arcs stay circular in the B-rep. Subtraction reverses the retained cutter wall to face the empty cavity.

cases.title: A plate with two through-holes
cases.b: B: radius-3 cylinders at (6,8) and (14,8), Z [−2,10] mm
cases.detail: B is a union of two separate cylinders. Subtraction makes two inner loops in each cap and two cylindrical cavity walls. The result is one connected plate; intersection has two bodies.

cases.title: Two crossing cylinders
cases.a: A: radius 4, axis Z, Z [−6,6] mm
cases.b: B: radius 2.5, axis X, X [−6,6] mm
cases.equation: x² + y² = 16; y² + z² = 6.25 ⇒ x² − z² = 9.75
cases.detail: The intersection is a spatial curve on both cylindrical walls. It is not one flat circle. The kernel maps the same curve into each cylinder’s angle/height domain before splitting and joining the retained surfaces.

cases.title: An oblique bore
cases.b: B: radius 2, length 24 mm; tilted 30° about Y; centred at (0,0,4)
cases.detail: The tilted cylinder is no longer a Z-prismatic solid. Plane/cylinder intersection curves become ellipses on the caps. Map each curve into both face domains, split them, then classify and stitch the selected patches.
